restatements.text: Establishes the text as the 2026 Billionaire Tax Act.
Provides the short title for the measure.
Details findings and declarations regarding healthcare, education, food assistance funding shortfalls, and wealth inequality.
States the purpose of the measure is to raise revenue for healthcare, education, and food assistance through a one-time wealth tax on billionaires.

Amends the California Constitution to authorize a one-time wealth tax, creates the 2026 Billionaire Tax Reserve Fund, exempts it from certain appropriation limits, and prohibits borrowing or transferring its funds to the General Fund.
Allocates 90% of the Reserve Fund to healthcare and 10% to education and food assistance, allows legislative appropriation of these funds, and requires annual reporting by the Department of Finance.
Names the added Revenue and Taxation Code section as the 2026 Billionaire Tax Act.
Imposes a one-time 5% excise tax on the net worth of applicable individuals and trusts with a net worth of $1 billion or more for the 2026 tax year, and details filing and payment requirements.
Defines how genuine debts and liabilities are taken into account and limited when determining net worth.
Establishes detailed rules for valuing different types of assets, including specific multipliers for business entities and exclusions for certain retirement accounts and property.
Creates an Optional Deferral Account system to allow qualifying liquidity-constrained taxpayers to defer payment until assets are withdrawn or transferred.
Sets requirements for certified appraisals and authorizes penalties for appraisers who make substantial or gross overstatements or understatements.
Establishes standard and alternative apportionment methods for the tax between multiple jurisdictions.
Allows a credit against the tax for taxes paid on net wealth in other jurisdictions based on residency.
Defines key terms for the Act, including applicable individual, applicable trust, net worth, tax obligation date, and valuation date.
Grants the Franchise Tax Board authority to adopt regulations, identify abusive transactions, and administer the tax without following standard administrative rulemaking procedures until 2028.
Permits the Legislature to amend the Act by a two-thirds vote if the amendment is consistent with and furthers the Act's purposes.
Provides a severability clause and directs courts to preserve the tax through limited adjustments if any part is found legally defective.
Imposes penalties of 20% or 40% for substantial or gross understatement of tax, establishes anti-avoidance rules, and allows the Franchise Tax Board to hire outside experts.
Directs that the provisions of the Part be liberally construed to achieve its purposes.
Creates an expedited judicial review process and validation action in Sacramento County Superior Court for facial challenges to the Act.
Prohibits taxpayers from deducting the net worth tax from their state income taxes.
Specifies that if this measure and another conflicting measure appear on the same ballot, the one with more votes prevails in its entirety.
Grants standing to the proponent and any citizen to defend the legality of the Act in court if the Attorney General does not.

evidence.quote: the fair market value of those interests at the end of any tax year shall be presumed to be the sum of the book value of the business entity according to generally accepted accounting principles as of the end of the tax year plus a present-value multiplier of 7.5 times the annual book profits
evidence.why: It introduces highly complex rules for valuing non-publicly traded businesses based on book value, accounting principles, and profit multipliers.

evidence.quote: An excise tax is imposed for tax year 2026 on the activity of sustaining excessive accumulations of wealth by applicable individuals with net worth of $1 billion dollars ($1,000,000,000) or more
evidence.why: It imposes a new tax explicitly and exclusively on individuals with the highest wealth, making them pay a larger overall tax share.

evidence.quote: The Board shall examine all returns submitted in accordance with this Part and shall determine the correct amount of the tax under this Part. The Board shall also examine all certifications or returns of taxpayers when the Board reasonably believes the taxpayers should have paid the tax imposed by this Part. Without limiting any other powers of the Board, in examining the returns made by taxpayers and examining whether returns should have been made by taxpayers but were not, the Board has all powers provided in Section 19504.
evidence.why: It expands the powers and auditing reach of the Franchise Tax Board to enforce the new wealth tax.

evidence.quote: Ninety percent shall be allocated to the Billionaire Tax Health Account for health care funding, which may include expenditures to restore or address any reductions in federal funding or state appropriations; investments to protect or enhance Medi-Cal and other health coverage programs for low-and moderate-income individuals
evidence.why: It dedicates massive new funding specifically to protect and enhance Medi-Cal and other health coverage programs.

evidence.quote:
Upon enactment of the 2026 Billionaire Tax Act and each fiscal year thereafter that the Reserve Fund is in existence, the Department of Finance, in consultation with relevant state agencies, shall provide to the Legislature all the following information:
(1) The current balance in the Reserve Fund as of the reporting date;
evidence.why: It requires the Department of Finance to provide annual reports and certifications to the Legislature regarding the new tax fund's balance and expenditures.

evidence.quote: Moneys deposited into the Reserve Fund shall only be used for the specific purposes provided by law. Action shall not be taken that permanently or temporarily changes the status of the Reserve Fund or borrows, diverts, or appropriates the moneys in the Reserve Fund in a manner inconsistent with this subdivision.
evidence.why: It guarantees that the tax revenue is earmarked exclusively for specific accounts and prohibits diverting it elsewhere.

evidence.quote: Notwithstanding any other law, the Reserve Fund is a special fund, permanently separate and apart from the General Fund or any other state fund or account. The taxes and the moneys resulting from the Act shall not be considered to be part of the General Fund
evidence.why: It locks the new tax revenue into a special fund, explicitly barring its transfer or use in the General Fund, thereby reducing budget flexibility.

evidence.quote:
Ten percent shall be allocated to the Billionaire Tax Education and Food Assistance Account for education-related and food assistance expenditures, which may include:
(A) Education-related expenditures to restore or address any reductions in federal funding or state appropriations, or to make investments to protect or enhance the kindergarten through grade fourteen public education system.
evidence.why: It allocates a portion of the tax revenue to protect and enhance public school funding from kindergarten through grade fourteen.

evidence.quote: The penalty for a substantial understatement under this Section shall be an amount equal to 20 percent of any understatement of tax.
evidence.why: It subjects taxpayers to large financial penalties if they understate the value of their wealth.

evidence.quote: The penalty for a substantial understatement under this Section shall be an amount equal to 20 percent of any understatement of tax.
evidence.why: It expands enforcement powers by creating new penalties against those who fail to accurately report the tax.

evidence.quote: All revenues from the Act-including taxes, interest, and penalties, and less refunds-shall be deposited in the State Treasury by the State Controller to the credit of the Reserve Fund.
evidence.why: It generates new money through a wealth tax to fund public services like healthcare, education, and food assistance.

evidence.quote: The Board shall examine all returns submitted in accordance with this Part and shall determine the correct amount of the tax under this Part. The Board shall also examine all certifications or returns of taxpayers when the Board reasonably believes the taxpayers should have paid the tax imposed by this Part. Without limiting any other powers of the Board, in examining the returns made by taxpayers and examining whether returns should have been made by taxpayers but were not, the Board has all powers provided in Section 19504.
evidence.why: It gives the Franchise Tax Board new powers and resources to examine returns and enforce the tax.

evidence.quote: An excise tax is imposed for tax year 2026 on the activity of sustaining excessive accumulations of wealth by applicable individuals with net worth of $1 billion dollars ($1,000,000,000) or more
evidence.why: It increases taxes paid by individuals who meet the wealth threshold.

evidence.quote: An excise tax is imposed for tax year 2026 on the activity of sustaining excessive accumulations of wealth by applicable individuals with net worth of $1 billion dollars ($1,000,000,000) or more
evidence.why: It applies exclusively to the highest wealth levels, making rates less equal across incomes.

analysis.answer: Current law was not provided. The measure introduces a new one-time 5% excise tax on the net worth of individuals residing in California with $1 billion or more in net worth. The revenue is directed to a new 2026 Billionaire Tax Reserve Fund.

There is a direct cost to billionaires who must pay the 5% tax. There are high compliance costs for taxpayers to appraise private assets and businesses, and large administrative costs for the state to audit returns and enforce the rules.

Individuals with a net worth over $1 billion pay the tax. Beneficiaries include low- and moderate-income individuals relying on Medi-Cal, state education, and food assistance, as well as the providers and systems handling those services. The Franchise Tax Board also receives start-up and operational funding.

Billionaires may attempt to reduce their taxable net worth through complex valuation strategies, shifting assets into exempt forms, or relocating themselves or assets before the valuation dates. The Franchise Tax Board will likely need to hire external experts and heavily audit complex returns.

The text asserts a problem of severe funding shortfalls for Medi-Cal, education, and food assistance programs, coupled with billionaires paying a smaller effective tax rate because their wealth grows untaxed. The mechanism—a 5% wealth tax dedicated to those specific programs—directly addresses both the revenue shortfall and the stated tax inequality.

The Franchise Tax Board gains significant discretionary power to enforce the tax, audit returns, and implement rules without following standard rulemaking procedures until 2028. The Legislature gains discretion over a massive new pool of special-fund revenue.

The economic effects of a wealth tax are highly disputed. Some researchers find that wealth taxes successfully reduce extreme inequality and raise substantial revenue. Others conclude that wealth taxes lead to severe capital flight, widespread tax evasion, reduced investment, and high administrative costs that wipe out the projected revenue gains.

Administration and enforcement costs will be exceptionally high. Valuing non-publicly traded businesses, trusts, and alternative assets is notoriously difficult and litigious. The text anticipates this by authorizing up to $50 million for the FTB's first year and permitting the hiring of outside legal and valuation experts.

Because the authorization for the tax and the fund structure are written into the California Constitution, undoing the core structure requires a subsequent ballot measure. The statutory components can only be amended by the Legislature with a two-thirds vote, provided the amendment 'furthers the purposes' of the Act.

flags.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of the Constitution, the Act provides for taxation on all forms of personal property and wealth
flags.note: Overrides other constitutional limits on taxing property or wealth.

flags.quote: The provisions of the 2026 Billionaire Tax Act, also referred to as "the Act," are severable.
flags.note: Includes a severability clause and directives for judicial reformation if parts are found unconstitutional.

flags.quote: The Legislature may amend the 2026 Billionaire Tax Act, by statute passed in each house of the Legislature by rollcall vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership concurring, if the statute is consistent with and furthers the purposes of the 2026 Billionaire Tax Act.
flags.note: Restricts legislative amendments to a two-thirds supermajority and limits them to furthering the Act's purposes.
